root_cause.text: The interrupt handler `interrupt_cnt_isr` was registered with the `IRQF_NO_THREAD` flag, but it acquires a spinlock_t (`counter->events_list_lock`) via `counter_push_event`, which is invalid in a PREEMPT_RT kernel because spinlock_t can sleep, causing a "BUG: Invalid wait context".
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `IRQF_NO_THREAD` from the `devm_request_irq` call in `drivers/counter/interrupt-cnt.c`. The commit message and CVE description include the lockdep warning showing the invalid context, and note that the handler cannot use both `IRQF_NO_THREAD` and spinlock_t.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes `IRQF_NO_THREAD` from the `devm_request_irq` call in `drivers/counter/interrupt-cnt.c`. The commit message and CVE description include the lockdep warning showing the invalid context, and note that the handler cannot use both `IRQF_NO_THREAD` and spinlock_t.

candidates.rationale: This line sets the IRQ_NOAUTOEN flag, which disables automatic enabling of the interrupt. While not directly causing the vulnerability, it is part of the interrupt setup that may influence the handling context.

This line registers the interrupt handler interrupt_cnt_isr using devm_request_irq. It is the call that binds the handler to the IRQ, and without proper threading flags, the handler will run in atomic context.

This line specifies the IRQF_NO_THREAD flag, which prevents the interrupt handler from being threaded. In PREEMPT_RT kernels, this forces the handler to run in atomic context, making spinlock acquisition (via counter_push_event) invalid and causing a 'BUG: Invalid wait context'.
This line provides the device name and counter pointer as arguments to the registration. It is part of the registration call but does not directly contribute to the threading issue.
This line checks the return value of the registration. It is error handling code and not directly related to the vulnerability.
This line returns the error code if registration fails. It is not directly related to the vulnerability.
